identity.title: Manual Reactor Trip on Degrading Condenser Vacuum Due to Piping Failure

cause.proximate_text: The direct cause of the event was High Cycle Fatigue Piping Failure of 1-SD-TK-1A, "A" High Pressure Heater Drain Receiver High Level Divert Line, that caused damage to condenser tubes and degraded condenser vacuum. Contributing to this failure was high level divert line design and piping orientation and craftsmanship on the flat pipe cap end plate weld. Additionally, there was insufficient procedural guidance on performing detailed inspections on the High Pressure Heater Drain Receiver High Level Divert Lines.
cause.theme: High-cycle fatigue piping failure due to design/orientation and weld craftsmanship, compounded by inadequate inspection procedure guidance

nodes.display_name: Condenser tube damage from pipe cap impact
nodes.description: The broken pipe cap damaged tubing in the "G" section of the tube bundle in the "A" Condenser Waterbox.

nodes.display_name: Air ingress causing condenser vacuum degradation
nodes.description: Tube damage allowed air ingress when the "A" Condenser Waterbox was isolated, causing degrading condenser vacuum.

nodes.display_name: MSR Flow Control Valve limit switches misadjusted
nodes.description: 1-MS-FCV-104NB/C indicated mid position with control switch CLOSED and controller demand at 0% following the trip; limit switches were adjusted/repaired.

nodes.display_name: Intermediate Range NI N-36 under compensated
nodes.description: One of two Intermediate Range Nuclear Instruments, N-36, was found to be under compensated during the reactor shutdown.
